decisions.decision: Excluded apps/v4/registry/_legacy-base-colors.ts (1,113 decls), apps/v4/registry/_legacy-colors.ts (1,200 decls), apps/v4/registry/themes.ts (840 decls) and apps/v4/app/legacy-themes.css (439 decls) from the declared token system.
decisions.moved: run.token_count from a raw discovery figure of 1,185 concepts down to 40 canonical tokens; single-source, coverage and orphans all graded against the smaller, real system instead of being swamped by catalog data.
decisions.other_reading: All four files are reachable from owned production entry points and declaration-shaped, so a stricter reading of 'discover every candidate, prove it ships' would inventory them as canonical sources the same as globals.css.

decisions.decision: Reported a deduplicated, collapsed canonical token count (40) as run.token_count, not the raw discover_tokens.py concept count for globals.css (93) or the theoretical alias_of-is-null count (35).
decisions.moved: The headline count away from double-counting Tailwind v4's own '@theme inline' pattern: 53 of the 93 raw concepts are same-file CSS-custom-property aliases (e.g. concept 'primary' and concept 'color-primary', the latter's sole value being 'var(--primary)') that discover_tokens.py's projection-collapse rule does not yet fold into their canonical concept — that rule currently covers only SCSS-to-CSS-custom-property compilation. This run applied that collapse by hand for tokens.filtered.json, merging each alias's site onto its canonical concept as a 'projected_from' entry. chart-1..5 (family 'color') were kept as their own canonical concepts rather than collapsed, because their alias target (--color-blue-300..800) is Tailwind's own default palette, not a name declared in this file — references/vitals.md's framework-default rule counts a project's own reference to a framework default as the project's token. font-sans/font-heading/font-mono were excluded rather than counted, because their @theme-inline declaration is self-referential (alias_of == its own id) — a passthrough for a next/font runtime-injected value, not a static definition.
decisions.other_reading: A stricter, literal reading of the tool's own concept list would report 93 (no collapsing) or 35 (collapsing only alias_of-is-null concepts, which would incorrectly also drop chart-1..5).

decisions.decision: Excluded 20 'canonical' concepts discover_tokens.py found outside globals.css (apps/v4/lib/font-definitions.ts, hooks/use-meta-color.ts, app/layout.tsx, app/(view)/preview/typeset/layout.tsx, and several font-loader helper files) from the token count.
decisions.moved: token_count away from counting non-token JS object properties as design tokens, and stack.token_sources down to the one file the project actually declares its design tokens in.
decisions.other_reading: Inspecting each: 'opengraph.width'/'opengraph.height' are literal OpenGraph image pixel dimensions (app/layout.tsx:45-46), 'icons.icon' is a favicon file path (app/layout.tsx:59), 'meta-theme-colors.dark'/'meta-theme-colors.light' are PWA theme-color meta values (hooks/use-meta-color.ts:5-6), and the rest (label/name/title/variable/registryvariable/previewvariable/value) are internal property names inside a custom font-loader's metadata records (lib/font-definitions.ts) — none is a name a component author would type in place of a value. The conservative-js-theme-object extractor currently has no shape heuristic to tell a real token map from an arbitrary data object; this is a tool limitation worth fixing, not a project finding.

decisions.decision: Graded leakage 'pass' rather than 'attention', though a real uncovered finding exists (#000000 x 24 in packages/shadcn/src/tailwind.css) and a large pool of literals (214 bracket-arbitrary px/rem values, near-miss overall) is unreviewed.
decisions.moved: The mechanical grade follows references/vitals.md's stated rule exactly: leakage's pass/attention/fail line reads only the redundant tier, and audit_literal_colors.py found zero redundant and zero exact-value-candidate findings across the 13 consumer stylesheets it scanned.
decisions.other_reading: A reader could reasonably want 'attention' here so the grade itself flags that something is unresolved, rather than relying on this note and the uncovered-tier listing to carry that signal — near-miss stayed unmeasured for color, and Tailwind bracket-arbitrary literals in .tsx (where the shimmer-color-[#378ADD] finding and the 214 unreviewed dimension literals both live) are outside what audit_literal_colors.py scans at all.

decisions.moved: mode-completeness to 'pass' with real file:line evidence, instead of 'blocked' — discovery.mode_resolution's own capability stayed unmeasured (the generic engine has no CSS-source-pairing check, only a build/runtime-artifact one), so a strict reading of the vitals.md instruction ('graded only where compiled or resolved output exists') would leave this blocked.
decisions.other_reading: references/vitals.md's mode-completeness signal is stated as 'the set difference across mode blocks' without requiring compiled output specifically (unlike coverage's framework-default rule, which is explicit about needing a checked version) — reading source blocks directly is a legitimate way to compute that set difference, and the original run against this same repository did the same thing.

adoption_strategy.headline: Unify decisions everywhere; unify components where ownership is proven.
adoption_strategy.rationale: This run found 1185 canonical concepts across 18 confirmed token-definition sources, 5 components with confirmed token usage, 2 active framework profiles, and 2 styling or framework adapters. A repository-wide component replacement would cross framework behavior and upgrade boundaries that this token audit does not measure. Use one semantic token contract across them, preserve framework-specific delivery adapters, and reserve shared component implementation for owned surfaces.

target_architecture.title: One canonical contract
target_architecture.description: Author one typed token graph for 1185 concepts; generate every other representation instead of maintaining parallel sources.

target_architecture.title: Semantic decisions
target_architecture.description: Map primitives to product intent such as text, surface, action, focus, and status. Require components to consume semantics by default.

target_architecture.title: Generated delivery adapters
target_architecture.description: Project the contract through tailwind, css-vars. Keep framework translation separate from the design decisions it carries.

target_architecture.title: Shared components for owned surfaces
target_architecture.description: Build versioned components for new and product-owned surfaces; let existing framework components adopt the same semantic contract without requiring shared markup.

target_architecture.title: Governance and proof
target_architecture.description: Version public contracts, deprecate before removal, validate every declared mode and production bundle, and reject regressions in CI.

integration_constraints.title: Framework and ownership boundaries
integration_constraints.evidence: 2 active framework profiles; 31 of 31 production roots are proven owned.
integration_constraints.implication: A global component replacement can turn upstream upgrades into long-lived fork maintenance. Preserve framework-owned behavior and markup until a component-contract assessment proves a safe boundary.

integration_constraints.title: Multiple delivery mechanisms
integration_constraints.evidence: 18 confirmed token-definition sources feed 2 styling or framework adapters.
integration_constraints.implication: Unify the decisions in one typed graph, then generate compatible projections. Requiring every framework to share one runtime format would couple design governance to implementation history.

integration_constraints.title: Behavioral contracts exceed styling
integration_constraints.evidence: 5 components with confirmed token usage; behavior, public APIs, localization, state, analytics, authorization, and interaction accessibility remain outside this audit.
integration_constraints.implication: Token adoption can align visual decisions without proving that shared component code is interchangeable. Assess those contracts separately before consolidation.

integration_constraints.title: Runtime modes need compiled proof
integration_constraints.evidence: 2 modes are declared and 0 bundle-by-mode pairs are resolved.
integration_constraints.implication: Source declarations prove intent, while compiled or runtime values prove delivery. Keep mode claims blocked until every production pair has evidence.

integration_constraints.title: Migration requires governance
integration_constraints.evidence: Enforcement is graded not-visible and 4 capabilities remain blocked or unmeasured.
integration_constraints.implication: A token package alone will not stop new drift. Pair migration with ownership, versioning, deprecation, CI gates, and measurable exit criteria.

standards.name: Design Tokens Format Module 2025.10
standards.role: Typed, tool-independent token interchange, aliases, groups, and deprecation metadata. Stable Community Group report intended for implementation; not a W3C Recommendation.

standards.name: CSS Custom Properties for Cascading Variables Level 1
standards.role: Runtime web projection for decisions that participate in the cascade or change by theme.

standards.name: WCAG 2.2
standards.role: Accessibility acceptance baseline for resolved color, focus, target, text-spacing, and motion outcomes; token presence alone does not prove conformance.

standards.name: Semantic Versioning 2.0.0
standards.role: Versioning and deprecation policy after the public token or component contract is declared.

rollout.title: Prove the boundary
rollout.objective: Resolve production reachability, ownership, and the evidence gaps that would make later adoption claims unreliable.
rollout.evidence: 1 unresolved import; 4 capabilities still blocked or unmeasured.
rollout.exit_criteria: Every actionable import is resolved or explicitly exempted, production roots are proven, and remaining unknowns are named as unmeasured.

rollout.title: Freeze identity and semantics
rollout.objective: Confirm brand identity, then define primitive, semantic, and optional component tiers with ownership and mode policies.
rollout.evidence: Typography identity is not-visible; brand color identity is not-visible.
rollout.exit_criteria: Every governed token has a type, description, owner, semantic role, and declared mode behavior.

rollout.title: Choose one source and generate adapters
rollout.objective: Make one token graph authoritative and generate runtime, legacy, and framework-specific projections.
rollout.evidence: 1185 concepts currently span 18 token-bearing sources and 2 adapters.
rollout.exit_criteria: No projection is independently authored, aliases resolve without cycles, and primitive-to-consumer lineage is traceable.

rollout.title: Prove modes and bundles
rollout.objective: Compile or resolve every declared mode across each production bundle and verify the resulting values, not only their source declarations.
rollout.evidence: 2 declared modes; 0 resolved bundle-by-mode pairs. No declared mode mechanism or resolved output was inspected.
rollout.exit_criteria: The coverage matrix contains no unexplained blocked cell and every declared mode has compiled or runtime evidence.

rollout.title: Migrate by impact
rollout.objective: Pilot the semantic contract on the highest-usage owned component or production surface; replace only decisions whose semantic role is proven.
rollout.evidence: 5 components using tokens was measured; start with v4 / chart-area-interactive.
rollout.exit_criteria: The pilot passes visual, accessibility, mode, and regression checks without changing component behavior or public APIs.

rollout.title: Enforce and expand
rollout.objective: Prevent new drift, publish deprecation rules, and expand shared components only where ownership and component contracts are proven.
rollout.evidence: Enforcement is graded not-visible; leakage baseline: redundant 0, exact-value candidate 0, near-miss not-visible, uncovered not-visible, uncovered candidate 1.
rollout.exit_criteria: CI rejects invalid aliases, missing modes, inaccessible resolved pairs, unapproved literals, and public removals without deprecation.

guardrails: Keep one hand-authored source of truth; generate every projection.
Consume semantic tokens by default and document every primitive exception.
Treat framework adapters as translation boundaries, not parallel design systems.
Prove every declared mode in compiled or runtime output before claiming coverage.
Never infer that token consistency proves component behavior or accessibility.
Version public contracts and deprecate before removing or renaming them.

success_metrics.target: one canonical authoring graph; every remaining source generated or mapped
every declared mode across every production bundle
all selected pilot components use semantic tokens
zero, with a CI rule preventing recurrence
verified, visible, mode-safe, and backed by source evidence

adoption_strategy.component_replacement_limit: This audit does not measure behavior, public APIs, localization, state, analytics, authorization, or interaction accessibility. Complete a separate component-contract assessment before proposing repository-wide replacement.
